title: Split pea toasts with rocket and capers

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Split peas, onion, garlic, capers, lemon, olive oil and bread are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every item, sourdough included, is an everyday line at Tesco at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a heavy pan, a masher, a bowl and a toaster or grill, and simmering and mashing are beginner technique.

works.reason: 200g split peas in 700ml water simmered for 45 minutes mashes to a thick purée for eight toasts, though a note to add a splash more water if it catches would help.

honest_times.reason: 15 minutes covers chopping, slicing radishes, mashing and toasting, and the 45-minute cook matches the simmer.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item and seasoning is used, nothing unlisted appears beyond water, and sourdough is a fair name for crusty bread.

seasonal_feel.reason: A 100g pile of peppery rocket with radishes on warm toast is a proper spring lunch topping, not a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner can follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Pulses, fresh leaves and radishes on bread make a filling, wholesome lunch.
